newsitem.title: AUSTRIA: Austrian woman jailed for abusing adopted daughter.
newsitem.headline: Austrian woman jailed for abusing adopted daughter.

text.p: A Vienna court on Friday jailed an Austrian woman for five years for abusing her retarded adopted daughter for years and locking her in a coffin-shaped box for nights on end.

The woman, a former religious teacher named only as Ernestine K., 65, was charged with beating Maria, now 22, and frequently locking her in a garden shed with her hands tied and her mouth sealed with sticking plaster when she and her husband went out.
"She did not just torture Maria, but inflicted serious lasting damage," judge Peter Straub told the court. "For years she carried out torture...in an inconceivable fashion."
Ernestine said just before the verdict was read out that she regretted locking up her daughter -- the only charge she accepted -- saying she thought it would make Maria grow.
"I am very sorry that I bought the box, but I did it hoping it would help Maria. When I hear that she suffered so much I am sorry," she said.
The court handed her husband Walter a 20-month suspended jail sentence for abuse and incarceration. Family friend Irmengard M. received a year's suspended sentence for failing to help the child.
The couple, who had had no children of their own, had adopted or fostered seven children over the years.

Dorit J., 43, the first foster child in the family, recently wrote a book entitled "The Unwanted Child" in which she claims she was frequently locked in the toilet or the living room and tied to the coffee table.
Sabine, 26, who was adopted as a child by the couple, testified that she had witnessed the abuse of Maria and watched her suffer for about 10 years.
"I was a coward...I studied and had a nice life. But I did not want to be an accomplice to murder," she said.
Last summer, Sabine alerted the Vienna authorities to Maria's ordeal in an anonymous letter and the girl was taken away from the family's home in a Vienna suburb.
The wooden box in which Maria spent many days and nights was found smeared with excrement and urine and contained blood-stained newspapers inside, prosecutors said.
The box, measuring 160 cm by 55 cm and 33 cm deep, (64 inches by 22 and 13.2 deep) with 14 holes for air and a bolt on the outside, was displayed in court during the three-day trial.
Maria who is undergoing psychiatric treatment, said in a video testimony played in court on Wednesday, that she had been terrified of "Mummy".
Asked what "Mummy" used to do, she said: "She beat me, kicked me in the stomach, pulled my ears and tore my hair."
Maria said her mother would lock her in the box as punishment "for wanting more food or for talking too much".
